title: We Cut 94% of AI Coding Tokens With a Local Code Index - Rajkumar Sakthivel, Tesco
talk_summary: A Tesco engineer found 90% of AI coding cost is input context, not output, and built a local hybrid (semantic + keyword) code index that returns only relevant code snippets, cutting tokens 94% on a benchmark. Key mechanisms: dual search to cover each other's blind spots, a cheap scoring formula instead of an LLM judge, and a shared index/memory across tools.

takeaways.technique: Local hybrid code index to shrink input context
takeaways.what_they_do: Index the repo into function/class-level pieces, run semantic and keyword search in parallel, merge results, and send only the top-scored snippets instead of whole files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of sending whole files, the AI search and index. It gets back only small piece of code actually it needs.
takeaways.numbers: 83K -> 4.9K tokens/question (94% less); 523 tokens with compression; 90% retrieval accuracy on FastAPI 53-file benchmark

takeaways.what_they_do: Measured that ~90% of spend is input tokens; output compression saved only ~8% total, so they targeted context size.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 90% of your AI cost is input... if you cut input by 94%, you can save about 61% total.
takeaways.numbers: 90% input / 10% output; 75% output cut = ~8% total savings

takeaways.technique: Cheap scoring formula instead of LLM relevance judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Score retrieved results with a fixed weighted formula (50% semantic, 30% keyword, 20% recency) and drop low scores, avoiding an extra model call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Some simple formula, 50% meaning score, 30% keyword score, 20% how the recent code is... runs 0.4 milliseconds, no extra AI calls
takeaways.numbers: 0.4ms scoring; LLM judge added 2-3s per query

takeaways.what_they_do: One shared index and persistent project memory so every tool/session reuses the same context instead of re-explaining the codebase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We built one shared index so all your tools connect to it... We explain the code base once. Every tool remembered.

takeaways.what_they_do: Benchmarked on a real open-source repo with 20 real developer questions, comparing baseline full-file context vs indexed retrieval, and tracked per-query savings against model price.
takeaways.numbers: 247 queries, 12.4M tokens saved, ~$186; 84% of savings from search layer

takeaways.technique: Honest limits: recall drops on multi-purpose files
takeaways.what_they_do: Reported that retrieval recall collapsed on large mixed codebases where files do many things, and chose a small fast model over a bigger one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We tested on large projects with 396 files. The recall dropped almost zero. If your files each do one thing, it works well.
